fields.AN_Notes: Other_Task: AI-driven hiring decisions and facial recognition, outside social work. The paper reports its own regression on AI hiring scores (gender as predictor, Direct_Discrimination) and an ANOVA of facial recognition error rates by gender and race (Disparate_Performance, Black women highest, Intersectional). The provenance of the hiring data, the facial recognition datasets and the survey sample is not documented in the text, and the figures closely follow the cited Gender Shades pattern; the empirical study type is coded as reported but its evidential quality is doubtful and should be checked by domain experts. Gender is coded binary (Male=1, Female=0) in the analysis and combined with race; no explicit statement that gender is socially produced. Mitigation (inclusive and diverse training datasets, bias audits, participatory design, diverse teams, policy) is recommended only; the survey measures perceptions, not an intervention.

fields.AN_Notes: Critical commentary proposing two feminist assignments for a university economics classroom. General_Guidance strategy verbatim: 'Students could enter such a prompt, or experiment with rephrased prompts as in Figure 2, then critically examine ChatGPT's generated paragraphs'. Gender bias in generative models and patriarchal value systems are only cited (Bolukbasi et al. 2016, Prabhakaran et al. 2022), so no bias axis and no Gender category are coded; race, class and gender appear only as social location in a reflection task about globalisation. The work's own bias example concerns definitions biased toward mainstream economic thinking, an epistemic and disciplinary bias rather than a social axis, so no harm type is coded. Mitigation is the proposed teaching practice of critical citation, not evaluated.

fields.AN_Notes: Prompt experiment on GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and GPT-4o with American and North Korean nationalities crossed with six mental disability states in five everyday scenarios, regular and flipped Likert scales and requested explanations. Bias is operationalised as willingness ratings; the authors call the interpretation of bias subjective, so the understanding is implicit. Mental disability is coded as Disability, the axis the work names. The intersection is nationality with mental disability, without gender. Outputs are attitude ratings, not allocations, so the harms are representational. The training-level recommendation (account for a spectrum of mental disability symptoms at data training and model engineering levels) is proposed future work. No social work setting; Soziale_Arbeit coded nein because the work addresses stigma in LLM output, not social work practice or its clients.

fields.AN_Notes: Invited commentary on ChatGPT in social work research. General_Guidance strategy verbatim: 'develop prompts that explicitly ask to identify the work of BIPOC scholars and resources and perspectives from underrepresented communities'; the paper also asks authors to disclose how the LLM was used with prompts. Bias axes from the work's own argument: white-centric content and BIPOC authors (Race_Ethnicity), Eurocentric content, authors from the Global South and mainstream white English (Language_Culture). The list race, gender, sexuality, ability, caste is an enumeration and is not coded. Mitigation: inclusive prompting and an ethical framework by the professional organisations, proposed. Task: research uses (research questions, qualitative themes, transcript editing, manuscript feedback); reviewing case notes for biased language is described as a research use.

fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual essay applying intersectionality, Black feminist thought, queer theory and critical race theory to AI. The risk assessment (ProPublica) and ImageNet examples are cited cases and are not coded as harm types; the age, disability and ableism terms appear only in a cited quotation. The work's own argument is that normative algorithmic categorisation constrains identities that are not easily categorised (Exclusionary_Norms). Axes follow the work's own worked examples: women of color, mixed race, trans, bisexual, femme and queer communities. Non_Binary_Inclusive is coded because trans and femme communities enter the argument as categories beyond the binary; this is a conceptual, not a measured analysis. Mitigation: intersectional strategies at data, design and implementation stages, community methodologies and the Data Nutrition Label as a data-collection example, proposed. Other_Task: artistic and tactical media practice with AI (the ladymouth chatbot, creative coding). Gender definition coded Explicit through the adopted queer-theory determination that female is not a clearly defined natural category.

fields.AN_Notes: Higher-education framework of Critical AI Literacy skills under an EDIA lens with suggestions for staff. General_Guidance strategies verbatim: 'engage in equitable and inclusive prompting when required', 'Use the same/different prompt(s) several times with the same/different tool(s) and compare the outputs to identify and mitigate potential (cultural) bias', 'Engage in a conversation with AI to challenge detected biases', 'prompting for inclusivity'. The axes gender, cultural, disability and racial bias appear only as an enumeration and are not coded. Exclusionary_Norms rests on the framework's own claim of epistemic injustice and the non-inclusive nature of AI outputs; the harm is asserted rather than demonstrated. Mitigation: inclusive prompting practice and staff education and curriculum embedding, proposed.
